summary: Intermittent runner SSH auth failures when Vault SSH rekey cron overlaps runner boot window
description:
Issue summary: Intermittent failures during nightly release warmup where ephemeral CI runners fail SSH authorization during job startup. Failures started after Vault SSH key rekey cron was changed to a more aggressive cadence.

Observed behavior: Between 02:20 and 02:40 UTC on 2026-03-10 two consecutive nightly release warmups experienced ~12% of ephemeral runners failing to accept SSH connections (connection refused or auth failure). Affected jobs either retried and succeeded after ~30s or timed out and needed manual requeue.

Impact: Nightly release pipeline warm-up can be delayed, slowing canary rollouts and producing noisy pager alerts. No customer-facing API impact observed, but internal release windows slipped by ~15-30 minutes on affected nights.

Relevant context: We recently deployed a change to Vault operator cron that rotates SSH host keys and rewraps authorized_keys entries for ephemeral-runner service accounts. The new schedule overlaps with the runner bootstrap window for nightly releases due to DST adjustments and an earlier scheduled warmup.

Key artifacts attached in logs field below and cross-references to related runbook and Slack thread.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule Vault SSH rekey cron to run at 02:25 UTC for us-east Vault cluster
2) Trigger ephemeral runner pool warmup for nightly release between 02:20–02:35 UTC
3) Observe intermittent 'permission denied (publickey)' and 'connection reset by peer' in runner-manager logs and job controller failures
4) Verify Vault rotated host key and replaced entries in runner authorized_keys during same window
impact: Affects internal release warmups and can block canary rollouts; ~10-15% of ephemeral runners fail bootstrap during overlap windows leading to pipeline retries and manual intervention.
logs: runner-manager[2026-03-10T02:24:17Z] WARN ssh: rejected key for user ci-runner: signer mismatch
vault-operator[2026-03-10T02:25:05Z] INFO started ssh-hostkey-rekey job: rewrap_authorized_keys count=78
kube-controller[2026-03-10T02:25:32Z] ERROR pod/ephemeral-runner-abc123 failed liveness probe: ssh auth failure
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Host key rotation and authorized_keys rewrap are not atomic with respect to runner bootstrap; transient mismatch between client-known host key and server presented key causes SSH client to fail connection or human operators to see host key warning and reject connections.
Checked Vault audit logs: rekey job completed between 02:25:03 - 02:25:08 UTC; rewrap operation reported 78 modified entries (matches number of active ephemeral runners at that time).
Correlated runner-manager logs: highest spike in ssh auth errors at 02:24:50 - 02:25:40 UTC overlapping with rekey window.

Observed configuration drift: runner bootstrap uses a short-living known_hosts cache populated at boot. When host keys change mid-boot, bootstrap SSH handshake rejects new key because it doesn't match cache, causing immediate job failure before retry logic runs.
Reproducer on staging: ran staged rekey during controlled warmup -> reproduced 9/50 failed boots (18%).
We verified that fallback retries eventually succeed once runner completes a fresh known_hosts reconcile or operator manually restarts runner pod.
comments: Avery Chen (2026-03-10): Escalating because nightly releases are blocked when this hits. Suspect timing collision introduced by Vault cron change from 03:00->02:25 UTC.
Marcus Patel (2026-03-10): I've taken ownership. Will collect logs from the runner-manager and coordinate with Vault team to get exact rekey timestamps.

Elena Ruiz (vault-operator) (2026-03-11): Confirmed the cron was changed in infra PR 4821 to reduce time-to-rotate. We can shift back if needed. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821

Marcus Patel (2026-03-11): As mitigation, I've added a 2-minute jitter to runner boot scheduling and enabled a known_hosts reconcile hook to run before job acceptance. Monitoring for next nightly run.
SRE Pager (2026-03-12): Observed reduced failure rate in next run (failed boots dropped to ~2%).
root_cause_analysis: The Vault SSH host-key rotation and authorized_keys rewrap job is non-atomic relative to ephemeral runner bootstrap. The rotation occurred while runners were performing known_hosts and authorized_keys validation, causing transient host key mismatches and client-side rejection. A scheduling change to the Vault cron without considering the runner warmup window introduced the collision.
workaround:
1) Add scheduling guard: avoid running Vault rekey jobs during release warmup windows (02:15–02:45 UTC).
2) Manual remediation: restart failing runner pods or trigger known_hosts reconcile script on affected pods.
3) Enable runner manager retry/backoff to allow automatic recovery (already applied as emergency config).
resolution_summary: Short-term: Applied a temporary schedule exclusion for Vault rekey to avoid the 02:15–02:45 UTC release warmup window and enabled known_hosts reconcile during runner bootstrap. Long-term: Implement an atomic swap strategy in the Vault operator (write new keys and flip symlink/flag after rewrap completes) and add a pre-rotation telemetry check to ensure no active runner warmups. Proposed infra PR to follow.
postmortem_actions: ACTION-1: Infra to implement atomic rewrap flip in vault-operator (owner: Elena Ruiz) - target ETA 2026-03-19
ACTION-2: CI/Release team to update warmup schedule config to publish warmup windows to infra scheduler (owner: Marcus Patel) - target ETA 2026-03-16
ACTION-3: Add known_hosts reconcile as a standard bootstrap hook for ephemeral runners (owner: DevEx: Priya Kapoor) - target ETA 2026-03-17
ACTION-4: Add an alert that correlates rekey runs with runner bootstrap failures to catch regressions (owner: Observability team) - target ETA 2026-03-20
sra_notes: Security review: no key material exfiltrated; rotation performed by internal operator with KMS-wrapped keys. Vault audit logs reviewed and preserved for compliance.
final_status: Monitoring after mitigation - reduced failure rate; pending infra PR for permanent fix
